title: How many glasses of milk does {{NAME_2}} drink?
description: {{NAME_2}} drinks half a glass of milk every day, and the video finds the glasses in a week and in January by multiplying the days by one half, the same way as the example in the book. It ends by checking the answers with pairs of days.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number of days times one half glass is that many halves, and two halves make one glass. Watch for students who count one whole glass for each day.

source: {{NAME_2}} drinks 1/2 glass of milk every day. How many glasses of milk does {{NAME_2}} drink in a week? How many glasses of milk did {{NAME_2}} drink in the month of January?
video_script.why: The child has multiplied a whole number by a fraction in the solved example and now uses the same step on a question about days.
video_script.substitution: Seven days of half a glass make seven halves, and two halves make one glass.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_2}} drinks half a glass of milk every day: how many glasses in a week and in January?
video_script.payoff_line: {{NAME_2}} drinks three and a half glasses in a week and fifteen and a half glasses in January

final_answer.value: 7/2 glasses (3 1/2) in a week and 31/2 glasses (15 1/2) in January
final_answer.spoken: three and a half glasses in a week and fifteen and a half glasses in January

video_script.fraction_reading: one half, seven halves, thirty one halves

names.{{NAME_2}}: drinks 1/2 glass of milk every day

maths_rules: days in a week = 7; days in January = 31
check: 2 days = 1 glass, so 7 days = 3 pairs and 1 day over, and 31 days = 15 pairs and 1 day over; a day over adds 1/2 glass
video_script.design: One idea: days times one half glass is that many halves. The glass cut into two halves and the strip of days are the anchor and stay all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a glass half full, and a calendar strip of days; a question mark over a week and over January

marks.scene: the small title card From your book appears
marks.ask: the calendar strip and the question marks appear

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about {{NAME_2}}.
<bookmark mark='drink'/>{{NAME_2}} drinks half a glass of milk every day.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many glasses does {{NAME_2}} drink in a week? And how many in the month of January?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a glass cut into two equal halves; one half is shaded as the milk of one day; a strip of 7 days for a week, and a longer strip of 31 days for January

marks.glass: the glass is drawn and cut into two equal halves
marks.days: the strip of 7 days and the strip of 31 days appear
marks.day: one half is shaded above each day

narration: <bookmark mark='glass'/>Picture a glass of milk cut into two equal halves.
<bookmark mark='days'/>A week has seven days, and January has thirty one days.
<bookmark mark='day'/>On each day, {{NAME_2}} drinks one half of a glass.

beats.on_screen: Given: milk each day = 1/2 glass; days in a week = 7; days in January = 31

marks.given: the given lines are written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, {{NAME_2}} drinks one half glass of milk every day.
A week has seven days, and January has thirty one days.

beats.on_screen: To find: glasses in a week and glasses in January

marks.find: the find line is written under the given lines

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the glasses of milk for a week and for January.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: glasses in a week = 7 × 1/2 = 7/2 glasses

marks.week: the line for a week is written

narration: <bookmark mark='week'/>Step one, find the glasses in a week, the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Seven days is seven times one half glass, so we multiply seven by one half.
Seven times one half is seven halves of a glass.

marks.jan: the line for January is written

narration: <bookmark mark='jan'/>Step two, find the glasses in January, which has thirty one days.
Thirty one days is thirty one times one half glass.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Thirty one times one half is thirty one halves of a glass.

beats.on_screen: Step 3 (check): 2 days = 1 glass; 7 days = 3 pairs and 1 day over; 31 days = 15 pairs and 1 day over

marks.check: the line 2 days = 1 glass is written
marks.seven: 7 days = 3 pairs and 1 day over is written
marks.thirtyone: 31 days = 15 pairs and 1 day over is written

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, check by pairing the days, because two days make one glass.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Seven days make three pairs and one day over.
<bookmark mark='thirtyone'/>Thirty one days make fifteen pairs and one day over.
Each day over adds one half glass.

marks.pay: both answers stay on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='week'/>Seven halves is three and a half glasses.
<bookmark mark='jan'/>Thirty one halves is fifteen and a half glasses.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>{{NAME_2}} drinks three and a half glasses in a week and fifteen and a half glasses in January.
